claim: Return decomposition assumptions: base EPS growth 15% a year with P/E de-rating from 38.3x to 28x (bull 18% and 32x; bear 9% and 20x), dividend yield 1.5%, dilution 0.5% a year; result about 9.0% a year (bull 14.8%, bear -3.3%), probability-weighted about 8%

author: valuation
claim: Scenario IRRs at INR 1,778.70 over 5 years: bear -7.9%, base 3.7%, bull 13.3%; E[IRR] (IRR of probability-weighted value plus dividends) 4.7%, mean of scenario IRRs 3.8%; margin of safety vs base range midpoint INR 1,244 is -43%; nominal asymmetry ratio 4.8
formula_or_inputs: scripts/valuation_tools.py scenario-irr on calc/valuation_scenarios.json (built by calc/valuation_build_scenarios.py from VAL-C044-C047, VAL-C026)

author: valuation
claim: Measured against the price compounded at the 11.7% hurdle (INR 3,090 in 5 years), probability-weighted shortfall is INR 884 vs excess INR 56 (hurdle-adjusted asymmetry 0.06); the bear case loses 33% including dividends (41% at the bear low end)
formula_or_inputs: sum p x max(V+FV(divs) - P(1+Ke)^5, 0) / sum p x max(P(1+Ke)^5 - V - FV(divs), 0); VAL-C049 inputs; calc/valuation_hurdle_asymmetry.json
notes: The tool's asymmetry ratio (VAL-C049) compares 5-year values with today's price without discounting, which flatters long-duration assets.
